heading: Overview of the CarbaQ CO2 Capture Unit
sectionPath: 1. Overview of the CarbaQ CO2 Capture Unit
summary: Process flow and main components of the CarbaQ unit.
markdown:
## Overview of the CarbaQ CO2 Capture Unit

Fermentation off-gas enters the unit through the foam trap, passes the activated carbon bed that removes odours and volatile organic compounds, and is compressed, cooled in the chiller and condensed into the receiver vessel.

An oxygen sensor monitors the purity of the gas before it is condensed.

Foam trap, activated carbon bed, compressor, chiller, receiver vessel. The heater keeps the gas above its dew point before the carbon bed.

The skid carries the compressor, the chiller, the carbon bed, the heater and the control cabinet with the HMI. The receiver vessel stands next to the skid.

CO2 displaces oxygen. Operate the unit only in a ventilated area with a CO2 monitor. The receiver vessel is a pressure vessel; never exceed its rated pressure.

Capture rate, electrical supply and receiver capacity are given on the data plate of the unit.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 1. Overview of the CarbaQ CO2 Capture Unit, page 3

heading: Attaching the Receiver and Setting the Back Pressure Regulator
summary: Receiver connection and BPR setting to 140 psi.
markdown:
## Attaching the Receiver and Setting the Back Pressure Regulator

Place the skid on a level floor near the fermentation vessels. Keep the inlet hose short and free of low points where foam can collect.

Connect the unit to the supply given on the data plate. The unit must be earthed.

Attach the receiver vessel to the liquid outlet of the chiller and open the receiver vent to purge air from the line.

The back pressure regulator (BPR) keeps the receiver at the pressure needed for liquefaction. Set the BPR so that Receiver Pressure reads 140 psi with the unit running.

Turn the BPR adjusting screw in steps of about 1/8 of a turn and wait for the pressure to settle after each step. Lock the adjusting screw when the value is reached.

Check all connections with leak detection spray before the first start.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, Preparing the Receiver Vessel, page 8

heading: HMI Alarms and Software Screens
markdown:
## HMI Alarms and Software Screens

The HMI shows the process screen, the trend screen and the alarm screen. The alarm screen lists active alarms with their time stamp.

The unit raises alarms for high pressure, high temperature, low oxygen purity and compressor faults. Shutdown alarms stop the compressor and must be acknowledged before restart.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 5. CarbaQ Software Components, page 15

heading: Replacing Activated Carbon
summary: When and how to replace the activated carbon.
markdown:
## Replacing Activated Carbon

Follow the maintenance intervals below. Record every maintenance action in the service log.

Replace the activated carbon when the VOC alarm occurs or after the interval on the data plate. Stop the unit and depressurize the carbon bed before opening it.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, Replacing Activated Carbon, page 17

heading: Calibration of Oxygen Sensor
summary: Monthly oxygen sensor calibration with ambient air.
markdown:
## Calibration of Oxygen Sensor

Calibrate the oxygen sensor monthly with ambient air as span gas. Moisture on the sensor causes drift; dry the sample line before calibration.

The O2 Percentage value on the HMI must read the span value within tolerance after calibration.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, Calibration of Oxygen Sensor, page 20

heading: Gas Quality Checks
summary: Sampling recovered gas for oxygen, VOC and moisture.
markdown:
## Gas Quality Checks

Take a gas sample from the receiver and analyse oxygen, VOC and moisture. A foam trap that is not emptied regularly raises the VOC content.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 8. Gas Quality Checks, page 24

heading: Moisture in sight glass
markdown:
## Moisture in sight glass

Problem: Moisture in sight glass

Cause: Condensate carried over from the chiller

Remedy: Drain the chiller separator and check the auto-drain valve.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 25

heading: Uneven gas flow into the unit
summary: Uneven gas flow; gas enters the unit in surges.
markdown:
## Uneven gas flow into the unit

Problem: Uneven gas flow; gas enters the unit in surges

Cause: Foam trap overfilled or a leak on the inlet hose

Remedy: Empty the foam trap and tighten the inlet hose connections.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 25

heading: Chiller High Pressure Shutdown - moisture in the carbon bed
summary: Chiller High Pressure Shutdown with moisture in the carbon bed.
markdown:
## Chiller High Pressure Shutdown - moisture in the carbon bed

Problem: Chiller High Pressure Shutdown with moisture in the carbon bed

Cause: Moisture reached the activated carbon bed

Remedy: Depressurize the unit, then dry or replace the carbon bed before restarting.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 25

heading: Receiver High Pressure Shutdown
markdown:
## Receiver High Pressure Shutdown

Problem: Receiver High Pressure Shutdown

Cause: Back pressure regulator set too high

Remedy: Lower the BPR setting and vent the receiver slowly.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 25

heading: Chiller High Pressure Shutdown - back pressure regulator
markdown:
## Chiller High Pressure Shutdown - back pressure regulator

Problem: Chiller High Pressure Shutdown

Cause: Back pressure regulator was moved

Remedy: Adjust the BPR about 1/8 of a turn at a time until Receiver Pressure reads 140 psi, then lock the adjusting screw. Allow up to 15 minutes for the pressure to settle after each step.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 25

heading: Compressor High Pressure Shutdown
markdown:
## Compressor High Pressure Shutdown

Problem: Compressor High Pressure Shutdown

Cause: Blockage downstream of the compressor

Remedy: Check the auto-drain and the check valve for blockage.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 25

heading: Heater High Temperature Shutdown
markdown:
## Heater High Temperature Shutdown

Problem: Heater High Temperature Shutdown

Cause: Heater thermostat fault or no gas flow

Remedy: Check gas flow and the heater thermostat.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 25

heading: Negative temperature but no liquid in the receiver
summary: Negative temperature but no liquid in the receiver.
markdown:
## Negative temperature but no liquid in the receiver

Problem: Negative temperature but no liquid in the receiver

Cause: Receiver insulation damaged or vent open

Remedy: Check the receiver insulation and close the vent valve.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 26

heading: Over pressurization of the compressor
markdown:
## Over pressurization of the compressor

Problem: Over pressurization of the compressor

Cause: Coalescing filter blocked or outlet valve closed

Remedy: Replace the coalescing filter; open the outlet valve.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 26

heading: Compressor false operation
markdown:
## Compressor false operation

Problem: Compressor false operation

Cause: Contactor, breaker or VFD fault

Remedy: Reset the breaker, check the contactor and the VFD fault log on the HMI.

sourceLinks.label: Fernwick Labs CarbaQ CO2 Capture Solution Operations Manual, 9. Troubleshooting Tips, page 26
